html:
SMTO-FIL-0041 — SMTO left an unfinished copy file alone because it couldn't confirm it

GUID: afe214ac-0377-4814-bf8b-df145a154078
Slug: file-transfer-ownership-mismatch
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to remove a leftover, partly copied file from a copy between Gateways, but the file or its folder had changed since SMTO made it. To avoid deleting something that isn't its own, SMTO left it in place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  2. In the destination folder, look for a file whose name starts with .smto-transfer- and ends with .partial (it may be hidden), but don't delete or move it. That is the leftover SMTO couldn't confirm, and it needs to be checked as it is.
  3. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details include the copy's number, which matches that leftover file's name.

What success looks like

  • After the Gateway's manager checks it, the leftover .partial file is gone and the destination file is correct.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the destination Gateway. Don't start the same copy again until they've confirmed what happened to the first one, and don't move or rename the destination folder in the meantime.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Transfer stage cleanup refused to unlink the stage because its name, pinned parent directory identity, or file device/inode/owner, type or link count did not match the journal's ownership record for that transfer.

What this means

  • Cleanup's stage path, parent identity or file identity/type/link-count fails the durable ownership proof for the exact registered transfer stage. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Cleanup's stage path, parent identity or file identity/type/link-count fails the durable ownership proof for the exact registered transfer stage.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the registered stage and current parent/inode identity; never remove a lookalike partial file by name alone.

How to fix it

  • On the destination Gateway, compare the .smto-transfer-*.partial file and its parent directory with the journal record (path, stage, identity, parent_identity) using stat; a moved or renamed parent, a replaced stage or an extra hard link causes this. Remove the stage manually only after confirming it is the orphaned stage and not the published destination; never bypass remove_stage's ownership checks.
  • Inspect the transfer's ownership evidence and current filesystem identities before any cleanup; do not bypass the ownership checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Cleanup proceeds only when the exact owned stage is proven, or the mismatch remains for operator reconciliation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
